page.overview:
Who is Agahnim?

When Hyrule became besieged by an onslaught of terrible misfortunes, the King of Hyrule offered a reward to anyone who could put an end to these disasters. A mysterious stranger named Agahnim came and put an end to these troubles with a previously unknown magic. He was declared a hero and given the prestigious positions of chief advisor to the King and heir to the Seven Sages. Agahnim used this position and his mysterious magic to brainwash all of Hyrule's Soldiers, kills the King of Hyrule by reducing him to a skeleton, and make six of the Maidens, who were descendants of the Seven Wise Men (Sages), disappear to the Dark World.

Princess Zelda, the remaining last of the descendants, hides in the Sanctuary after being rescued by Link followed by her telepathic plea of help. She stays there until Agahnim's troops find her and take her to the tower at the top of Hyrule Castle. There, Agahnim sends her to the Dark World before Link could stop him, thus breaking the Seal of the Seven Sages. He gloats that nothing can stop him, because the Tribe of Evil is armed with the Triforce, and that evil and darkness will soon overrun the Light World. After this, he seemingly vanishes, but Link is able to quickly discover his whereabouts by slicing open a curtain and revealing a hidden chamber where he duels the Dark Wizard, turning his own magic against him. Before Link can soundly defeat him, however, Agahnim draws him into the Dark World. During his quest to rescue the Seven Maidens, Link learns that Agahnim is a servant, or perhaps a pawn, of Ganon.

When Link defeats Agahnim a second time at the top of Ganon's Tower, he ultimately collapses dead, and from his body a faint image of Ganon himself appears. The image turns into a bat and flees to the Pyramid of Power. At the start of the final battle, Ganon reveals that Agahnim was actually his alter-ego.

Even with the Master Sword, Link is unable to harm Agahnim directly. He must use the magical blade to turn his own magic attack against him to damage the evil wizard. If the young hero attempts to strike Agahnim's body with the Master Sword, he receives a violent electrical shock in consequence, including in its Tempered or Golden forms.
